name: Sonobot-5

placement_rationale.text: Moved from 60 km to 20 km, and the band tag from op_deep to op_near — 60 km exceeded the asset's own stated 30 km operating range (see key_facts/characteristics), an internal contradiction between the platform's real envelope and where it was placed. Sonobot-5 is a small EvoLogics-built hydrographic-survey/inspection catamaran supplied to Ukraine to inspect harbors and waterways and detect seabed ordnance with side-scan/multibeam sonar, not an open-water strike or deep-reconnaissance platform the way Magura V5 or MANTAS T-12 are — its documented real-world role is close-in coastal/port work, not the 100+ km depths those strike-optimized USVs reach. 20 km sits comfortably inside its own 30 km range with margin for a return transit, and inside doctrine.md §2's operational band depth rather than the deep-strike layer.

characteristics: Strength: Purpose-built for survey/reconnaissance rather than strike, complementing kamikaze USVs like Magura with a persistent-presence role
Limitation: Short range relative to strike-focused USVs like Magura V5
Estimated quantity available: Donated numbers not fully disclosed
employment_notes: Represents the reconnaissance/ISR layer of the naval drone ecosystem, paired conceptually with strike USVs the way air recon drones pair with FPV strike drones
contrast_vs_traditional: A small survey and reconnaissance USV does a job — hydrographic and reconnaissance work near a contested coastline — that traditional naval doctrine assigned to a crewed vessel operating under real risk of loss. An uncrewed platform removes that risk for exactly the kind of persistent, repetitive presence the doctrine.md pattern-of-life detection finding describes for ground reconnaissance, applied to the water instead.
